results.summary_before: Speck-V SoC is a TinyQV RISC-V system on chip with custom ISA extensions for the SPECK-ARX lightweight block cipher. It exposes UART, SPI, QSPI flash and PSRAM interfaces, GPIO, interrupts, and a debug UART, matching the QSPI Flash/PSRAM and SPI Pmod pinouts. It runs at 64 MHz and is intended as a microcontroller-class platform for lightweight cryptography workloads. The documentation provided here is limited to the title, pin names, and pinout match, so the custom instruction details and test results are not described.

results.summary_before: Project Long Man is a quasi-delay-insensitive die-to-die interconnect that streams data via SPI. It uses toggle-based encoding on TX/RX lines to reduce switching activity. The design can be tested by tying RX and TX together and controlling it through SPI signals. No external hardware is required.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-bit, 2-stage pipelined CPU with a custom ISA inspired by ARM, featuring four registers and thirteen instructions. It interfaces with an external byte-addressable 8-bit SRAM that must provide combinational read and a write enable signal. The CPU uses dedicated input, output, and bidirectional pins for data, address, and control signals. The design requires an external SRAM chip to function and is intended for embedded processing tasks.

results.summary_before: This design implements a simple combination-lock puzzle that lights an output when a specific 8-bit input pattern is applied. The documentation states that the display should show a 'y' only when inputs 3, 7 and 8 are high and all other inputs are low, and be blank otherwise. It is a Wokwi-based combinational logic project with no clock and no external hardware listed. The documentation is thin and the pin descriptions are informal, so the exact display behavior is inferred from the test description.
